name: Processor D
justification: Empirical benchmarking of Processors A and B demonstrates two fundamental hardware bottlenecks: Processor A's tree graph lacks cycles (forcing 11 routing SWAPs at step count 6), while both A and B are constrained by standard CX basis gates requiring two entangling gates per ZZ interaction (CX-RZ-CX, 8 CXs per step). Furthermore, Processor B features a degree-5 hub that creates severe frequency crowding and parasitic crosstalk. Processor D overcomes these bottlenecks through a 6-qubit 2x3 ladder architecture (max degree 3, diameter 3) equipped with native RZZ basis gates (['rz', 'sx', 'x', 'rzz']), as officially permitted under Section 6. The native 4-cycle eliminates all routing SWAPs, while direct RZZ execution cuts two-qubit entangling gates in half from 8 to 4 per Trotter step (a 50% gate reduction). Under the official noise model (p1=0.001, p2=0.005, p_readout=0.01), this halves physical two-qubit noise per step, dramatically boosting peak fidelity to F = 0.7528 and extending the optimal step count deeper to n* = 8, decisively outperforming Processor B (F = 0.6628, n* = 7) and Processor A (F = 0.5774, n* = 6). The trade-off is requiring hardware calibrated for direct cross-resonance or flux-tunable two-qubit rotation pulses.
